notes: Confirmed register ABI. Entry reads through x0, retains the low 32 bits of x1 as a selector, writes one byte via x2 and one 32-bit value via x3. Both indexed call sites explicitly initialize x2/x3 to byte/word stack output slots and x1 to 0 or 1. Return paths set x0 to 0 or 1; the first caller immediately tests that result, while the second consumes it as a condition. Generic pointees are appropriate; no recovered structure type is established.

The indexed caller sets only x0, then does not consume a result. The epilogue does not commit a deliberate x0 return. Keep the object pointer opaque because the observed offsets do not recover its source type.

Confirmed two pointer-shaped incoming registers. Entry reads x1+8 and dereferences the descriptor fields at x1+0 and x1+8, while x0 is retained as the tagged-value base and read for tag/control bytes. The indexed callers pass the tagged value in x0 and a stack descriptor in x1. Although one internal path computes a scalar in x0, the callers ignore post-call x0 and the function has other paths that return without setting it, so a source-level result is not established. Keep both pointees opaque.

recommended_prototype: void set_attribute_record_value(void *arg0, uint32_t arg1, uint32_t arg2)
notes: Confirmed three register arguments and void behavior. The body snapshots x0 as the record pointer, x1 as a 32-bit selector and x2 as a 32-bit value, then dispatches on the selector and forwards the value to byte/word write helpers. The indexed caller repeatedly sets x0 to the record, x1 to 0-3, and x2 to the corresponding 32-bit value. No deliberate return is established; the caller ignores x0. Keep the record pointee opaque.
